title: Henselization of a pair
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring and $J\subseteq B$ an ideal. Let $\mathcal C$ be the category whose objects are the etale ring maps $B\to C$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] (i.e. $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ etale) such that the induced map $B/J\to C/JC$ is an isomorphism, and whose morphisms are the $B$-algebra maps. Then: (1) $\mathcal C$ is essentially small and directed (nonempty, any two objects map to a common one, any two parallel morphisms are coequalized by a morphism); (2) setting $B^h=\varinjlim_{C\in\mathcal C}C$ and $J^h=JB^h$, the pair $(B^h,J^h)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]; (3) the map $B/J\to B^h/J^h$ is an isomorphism; (4) $(B,J)\mapsto(B^h,J^h)$ is left adjoint to the inclusion of henselian pairs into pairs. (For the use here only (1)-(3) are needed.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization) and its proof (directedness of $\mathcal C$, $A^h=\colim B$, $A/I=A^h/IA^h$); cited in this form in etale-cohomology.tex, proof of Lemma Tag 0A51
